bullets.text: Aggregate CR was 85.2 vs 85.0 last year; accident-year CR was 88.2, better reflecting current pricing and loss trends; margins remained well ahead of the 96 long-term target.

Companywide NPW grew 2% year-over-year, with reduced private passenger auto new applications contributing most significantly to results; Commercial Auto written premium grew about 14%, with new applications increasing.
Private passenger auto PIF grew about 2% in Drive and about 8% in Direct; Commercial Auto policy counts increased about 11% over the prior-year period.

Favorable prior-year reserve development continued at unexpected levels; Northeast winter conditions did not produce traditionally expected frequency; negative frequency trends continued by coverage, and severity trends were mostly positive but unremarkable.
Repurchased 2.2M shares; Board approved 4:1 stock split effective May 18, 2006; 2007 variable dividend will use Gainshare factor, which reached 1.54 through Q1 (January 1.55, February 1.46).
New private passenger auto applications slowed more in Drive Insurance than Progressive Direct; year-to-date premium per policy declined about 5% in Drive auto, but was about level in Direct.
Concierge Level of Claims Service completed three more service centers in March; openings will accelerate across Q2 and Q3, with expectations set at 29 new centers in 2006.

Characterized Q1 as 'Good, not great' based on growth attained relative to customer potential; company believes its market response is the correct balanced course, with operations and profitability on track.

Announced future departures of CFO Tom Forrester in Q1 2007 and Drive Group President Bob Williams in mid-May 2006; active succession planning provides opportunities for several qualified candidates to join management.
